A_core_direct_lifespan.title: Rapamycin fed late in life extends lifespan in genetically heterogeneous mice.
evidence_quotes: We report here that rapamycin, an inhibitor of the mTOR pathway, extends median and maximal lifespan of both male and female mice when fed beginning at 600 days of age.

For data pooled across sites, a log-rank test rejected the null hypothesis that treatment and control groups did not differ (p < 0.0001); mice fed rapamycin were longer lived than controls (p < 0.0001) in both males and females.

A_core_direct_lifespan.title: Health Effects of Long-Term Rapamycin Treatment: The Impact on Mouse Health of Enteric Rapamycin Treatment from Four Months of Age throughout Life.
evidence_quotes: At four months of age 160 mice, 80 animals per sex, began receiving mouse chow (Purina 5LG6) containing either microencapsulated rapamycin (14 ppm) or empty capsules (eudragit = control), (n = 40 animals per sex and treatment group).
Consistent with our previous findings, survival of both males and females was modestly enhanced in YF animals [ 35 ].

A_core_direct_lifespan.title: Transient rapamycin treatment during developmental stage extends lifespan in Mus musculus and Drosophila melanogaster.
evidence_quotes: Rapamycin (10 mg/kg) was administered daily in two distinct temporal windows, from postnatal day 4 to postnatal day 30 (P4‐P30), or from postnatal day 30 to postnatal day 60 (P30‐P60)
Combined data from both sexes showed a 9.6% increase in median lifespan in P4‐P30 rapamycin‐treated mice compared with control mice (treated with ethanol)

A_core_direct_lifespan.title: Transient rapamycin treatment can increase lifespan and healthspan in middle-aged mice.
evidence_quotes: we set out to investigate whether a single three-month treatment regimen can extend lifespan and healthspan in C57BL/6JNia mice starting at 20–21 months of age.
After receiving the lower dose, both male and female mice lived about 50% longer than untreated mice, and showed improvements in their muscle strength and motor coordination.

B_disease_model_survival.title: Acarbose suppresses symptoms of mitochondrial disease in a mouse model of Leigh syndrome.
evidence_quotes: Furthermore, rapamycin and acarbose have additive effects in delaying neurological symptoms and increasing maximum lifespan in Ndufs4 −/− mice.

Daily administration of rapamycin, an inhibitor of the nutrient sensing mechanistic target of rapamycin complex I (mTORC1), rescues multiple manifestations of mitochondrial disease in Ndufs4 −/− mice, including neurological symptoms, accumulation of glycolytic intermediates and lactate, loss of body fat, aberrant nutrient and growth factor signalling, and survival

B_disease_model_survival.title: Rapamycin Reduces Carcinogenesis and Enhances Survival in Mice when Administered after Nonlethal Total-Body Irradiation.
evidence_quotes: Immediately after TBI, along with untreated control groups, animals were placed on chow containing different concentrations of encapsulated rapamycin (14, 40, 140 mg/kg chow).

Kaplan-Meier survival curves revealed that all three concentrations of rapamycin afforded a significant survival advantage by delaying the time at which tumors appeared and reduction of the incidence of certain tumor types such as hepatocellular carcinomas.

B_disease_model_survival.title: BMAL1-dependent regulation of the mTOR signaling pathway delays aging.
evidence_quotes: treatment with the mTORC1 inhibitor rapamycin increased lifespan of Bmal1−/− mice by 50%
we decided to compare activity of mTOR signaling in cells isolated from wild type and BMAL1-deficient mice

C_secondary_contextual.title: Rapamycin doses sufficient to extend lifespan do not compromise muscle mitochondrial content or endurance.
evidence_quotes: we tested whether rapamycin, at the same doses used to extend lifespan, affects mitochondrial function in skeletal muscle.
rapamycin-treated mice had endurance equivalent to that of untreated controls, and isolated, permeabilized muscle fibers displayed similar rates of oxygen consumption.
